jurisdiction.name: Group of Twenty
jurisdiction.overview: Forum of 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union, with a rotating presidency and no secretariat. Its texts are political commitments.

narrative.summary: The G20's AI text is the G20 AI Principles, annexed to the Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy adopted at Tsukuba on 8-9 June 2019 under Japan's presidency. Drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI, the principles cover inclusive growth, human-centred values and fairness, transparency, robustness and accountability; the statement says they are non-binding. The G20 has 21 members: 19 countries, the European Union and the African Union, which became a permanent member at the New Delhi summit of September 2023.
lead_institutions: G20 Trade and Digital Economy Ministers
narrative.review_notes: Membership is taken from Global Affairs Canada's G20 page (Canada is a G20 member and past host); the G20 presidency site and several past presidency sites could not be read. The African Union's accession is recorded from the New Delhi Leaders' Declaration of 9-10 September 2023 as published on the same Canadian government site, which gives no exact accession day. The AI Principles come from the PDF of the Tsukuba ministerial statement published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. Pending: the Osaka Leaders' Declaration (June 2019), in which leaders welcomed the principles, on Japan's foreign ministry site, which could not be read; and later G20 statements on AI.

instruments.current_status: Annex to the G20 Ministerial Statement on Trade and Digital Economy, headed 'G20 Ministerial Meeting on Trade and Digital Economy, June 8-9, 2019, Tsukuba, Ibaraki, Japan'; the month is recorded because the statement gives the two meeting days rather than one date. Paragraph 19: the ministers are 'guided by the G20 AI Principles drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI, which are attached in Annex and are non-binding'. The Annex says 'The G20 supports the Principles for responsible stewardship of Trustworthy AI in Section 1 and takes note of the Recommendations in Section 2.' Full text from the PDF published by Japan's Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications, one of the co-chairing ministries.
instruments.summary: Principles drawn from the OECD Recommendation on AI and welcomed by G20 trade and digital economy ministers in 2019. Section 1 sets five principles for responsible stewardship of trustworthy AI (inclusive growth, sustainable development and well-being; human-centred values and fairness; transparency and explainability; robustness, security and safety; accountability), which the G20 supports; Section 2 lists national-policy and international-cooperation recommendations, which the G20 takes note of. The text states that the principles are non-binding.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: AI principles endorsed at G20 ministerial level, extending the OECD AI Principles to G20 members that are not OECD adherents.

The 21 members are: African Union, Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, European Union, Germany, France, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, South Korea, Türkiye, United Kingdom, United States of America.' Only the 19 countries are listed in members; the EU and the AU are recorded in union_members.
